And that is creepy.

item.content:encoded:
Too on-the-nose for a regular entry. Honestly it could have made a good J-entry but as a normal one… no, sorry but no. It's just too goofy.

And don't get me wrong, I'm not saying all regular SCPs have to be creepy or serious, but this takes it way too far in the silliness, and that's coming from a guy who doesn't mind a bit of lolfoundation (as long as it's kept to a minimum and still works in-universe).

The mental image of an evil carnivorous cardboard box walking around on its flaps just doesn't seem like the tone the wiki is going for. It feels more like one of the sillier Dungeons & Dragons enemies than an SCP.

I almost wanted to upvote it for how hilarious it is but again, I don't think this is the kind of article we want to encourage for regular entries.

item.content:encoded:
I love the idea, and I upvoted it, but I think it still needs some work. My comments are below. I'm new so take them with a grain of salt:

Click Here.
Close
 When a subject enters SCP-647, the flaps of the box will close and are unable to be opened. In testing, the flaps resisted a force in excess of 30 kN.

Not sure why, but that sentence doesn't sound science-y. Maybe "the flaps of the box shut and seal securely." Not sure you need to put how strong they are.

 Once the flaps are closed, the object will secrete a digestive fluid. This fluid, unlike mammalian stomach acids, is a decaying agent that slowly weakens its victims from the inside out. From there, the body is dissolved and the bones are expelled from [DATA EXPUNGED].

I don't like the decaying agent, as it doesn't seem science-y. If it is supposed to be part of the anomalous properties (like its some unencountered magic-decay-fluid) then that should be stated.

 As the time since the last feeding increases, the transformation becomes more elaborate, including a blanket and lining of newspaper (after two days), cans of food (after three days) and bottles of alcoholic beverages (after five days).

I am quoting this only because I love it. The idea of a predator cardboard box trying to attract bums with booze is really funny and a tad bit eerie.

 Locomotion is achieved by means of movement of the flaps.

Don't think you need that. The image of this thing trying to shuffle around using its flaps breaks suspension of disbelief and makes it seem a little too absurd and stupid. Short range teleportation is probably too anamolous for something like this. You could probably leave out method of locomotion altogether. If you feel it is absolutely necessary, maybe have it shrink a little smaller and 'roll' like its caught in some imaginary breeze. Maybe it even creates an anamolous breeze for that purpose.

 SCP-647 has also been know to actively attack a subject rather than waiting for them to enter on their own. Attacks have been triggered by: Attempts to damage SCP-647 (including sample retrieval) Attempts to remove extra components manifested by SCP-647 Time periods of more than 7 days between feedings

I like the idea of this thing attacking. I have a mental image of some researcher holding a stool and cracking a whip, trying to keep it at bay.

 In addition, after eight days, SCP-647 will attempt to relocate. If blocked, it will spray a caustic liquid similar to its digestive juices onto all nearby objects (including walls), causing them to dissolve over fifteen to twenty minutes depending on composition and mass.

Unnecessary.

The rest is good stuff. I especially like how it needs whole, FRESH victims, for some nefarious, unknown purpose.

Fixed the collapsible for you. - Zyn

item.title: What really bugs me about this SCP...
item.content:encoded:
It's one of those "Critters that kill you by pretending to be an ordinary object that it hopes you will use." This one has been here a long time (and might be the original of that type) and I don't remember reading it before, but we had a flurry of them on the site a couple years ago. Something pretends to be a can of Coke, and when you drink it, you die and become a bunch of anomalous cans of Coke. A bottle of bubble bath that eats you if you take a bath with it. I thought these SCPs were on to something creepy, but there was a logical flaw here: You have some kind of living thing that can change form — obviously, not actually a box, or a can of soda, or whatever. Why would it always pretend to be the same thing? So I wrote SCP-157 to get around that problem.

I read this, and think: Well, it's just another instance of 157 on the loose that likes to attract homeless people. When it gets bigger, it'll pretend to be a discarded mattress or an old couch.
